Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps on the performance / SLO conversation so we have alignment going into sizing: 

Recap from call:
- Primary goal: support Finex’s document-assist product with streaming generation for user-facing summaries and Q&A.
- Target SLOs: 95th/99th token latency targets and first-token time are important — you called out 99th <= 300ms for interactive UX.
- Workload shape: steady background load with sharp marketing-event bursts (minutes) where traffic can spike 10–15x.
- Model family: you’re evaluating 13B-class open models (quantized) for cost reasons; may also want a smaller 7B variant as fallback.

What we need from you to size correctly:
1) Typical / average tokens per request and tokens per response (rough estimate is fine).
2) Steady-state QPS and expected peak QPS (burst QPS and typical burst duration).
3) Concurrent active sessions (if available) and any streaming requirements (first token target, sustained tokens/sec).
4) Example traffic logs or a 1–2 hour sample trace (anonymized) — we can ingest to produce a sizing estimate.

Attached: finex-sizing-template.xlsx (fill the simple worksheet with the numbers above) and our redwood-throughput-guidance.pdf for reference.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You: drop the filled template + sample logs into the Drive link or reply here by EOD Thu.
- Us: we’ll run a quick sizing analysis and return an initial capacity recommendation within 48 hours of receiving logs.
- Optional: 30-min follow-up call to review assumptions and recommended node counts.

Thanks — looping in Rafael and Marissa for sizing and ops input.

Best,

Neha — thanks for the clear notes. Answers below (rough numbers from product telemetry):

- Avg tokens per request (input + generation): ~800 tokens (typical user session 600 input / 200 generated).
- Steady-state QPS: 8 req/s (mostly daytime business hours).
- Peak QPS: ~120 req/s for marketing bursts, typically 3–7 minutes. We also see longer medium peaks (~30–45 minutes) at ~40–50 QPS.
- Concurrent active sessions: ~350 steady, up to ~5,000 during peak bursts.
- Streaming: yes — we need streaming with first token under 400ms and a sustained emission rate of ~20–30 tokens/sec.
- Model: planning to run a quantized 13B (4-bit) as primary; 7B fallback for extreme load.

I don’t have sanitized logs ready for sharing in this thread — I’ll upload a 1-hour sample trace to the Drive link by EOD. Also attaching a small CSV (summary) with per-minute QPS for last 7 days.

Perfect — this is exactly what we need. Quick notes based on your numbers: 

- Steady tokens/sec: 8 QPS * 800 tokens = ~6.4k tokens/sec.
- Peak tokens/sec during worst bursts: 120 QPS * 800 = 96k tokens/sec (short 3–7 minute bursts).
- Concurrency numbers line up with those bursts (5k concurrent sessions).
- Streaming first-token <=400ms and 20–30 tok/sec sustained is feasible, but tail guarantees at 99th will drive node count and model selection.

Next actions we’ll take once you upload the sample trace:
- Rafael will run the trace through our sizing tool to estimate required GPU capacity (tokens/sec per node, expected tail latency at your SLOs).
- We’ll produce two configs: a cost-optimized config (more batching / slightly higher latency) and an SLO-first config (lower latency, higher reserved capacity).
- Provide a recommended canary rollout plan (7-day) and fallback to 7B during extreme overloads.

Can you confirm the CSV/trace upload and whether Finex requires SOC2 data handling (we’ll treat samples as sanitized)? Also, is there any maximum acceptable cold-start time for model swapovers?

I’ll schedule a 30-min recap for Fri 10am PT unless you prefer another slot.

Thanks — Neha

Short internal sizing note based on Alex’s numbers (for Neha to share back):

Assumptions: primary model = quantized 13B, avg 800 tokens/request, streaming target first-token <=400ms, sustained 25 tok/sec.

Estimate (very rough, quick calc):
- Tokens/sec steady: ~6.4k. Peak short bursts tokens/sec: ~96k.
- If a single high-throughput GPU (A100-like) can sustain ~12k tokens/sec for the chosen quantized kernel under good batching, then:
  - Steady-state: 1 GPU could likely handle baseline load (6.4k) with headroom.
  - Peak (96k): ~8 GPUs required to absorb sustained peak token emission assuming ideal batching (96k / 12k =~ 8).
  - However, streaming and 99th-tail target means we should reduce batching depth for tail latency. With latency constraints, effective per-GPU throughput may drop to ~6–8k tokens/sec. Using conservative 8k tokens/sec: peak => 12 GPUs.

Recommendation to include in the customer deliverable: 
- Start with a 3-tier plan: (1) small baseline pool (2–3 GPUs) for steady traffic + autoscale headroom, (2) scheduled burst nodes (or burst autoscaling policy) to add 8–12 GPUs for marketing events, (3) a fallback small 7B fleet to degrade gracefully.
- Canary: run 1–2 GPUs in production for 48 hours with traffic shadowed to validate tail latency at 99th.
- We’ll ask Finex for a 1-hour trace; Rafael to run sizing script and return a spreadsheet with recommended node counts and cost estimate within 48 hours of trace.

I’ll draft the sizing spreadsheet once we have the trace. Thoughts?

-Rafael
